Best,

Ethan — thanks, sending a concise onramp plan below and attaching a sizing workbook. TL;DR: we recommend a staggered ramp over 6 weeks with an initial 40% reserved footprint (2/5 of final fleet) for smoke runs, then a 3-week load validation window, and a final 2-week steady-state run before DNS cutover. If 99th lat breaches, we have three throttles: (1) temporary routing back to hosted, (2) per-route rate limiting, (3) autoscale burst to shared capacity for short windows.

Attachment: arbor_onramp_capacity_runway_v1.xlsx (sheet: Week-by-week run-rate)

Next steps I propose: Jordan to validate throughput assumptions with infra, Marcus to draft the cutover checklist, and Karthik to confirm contractual SLA/commit language relevant to ramp. Can the team meet Thursday 10am PT to align?

—Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Reed <ereed@arborlabs.ai>, Nora Kim <nora.kim@arborlabs.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-23 08:36 PDT
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on Dedicated commit sizing — throughput validation notes

Folks — I ran Arbor's sample traces against our throughput model and sketched a conservative profile. Key notes:
- Chat model: sequence len 512 avg, top-k sampling; estimated token generation TTF of 1.8ms/token on A100-80GB quantized path.
- Embeddings: small transformer, cheap; can be colocated on CPU with batching if needed but we recommend keeping it on GPU for latency during cutover.
- Concurrency: to hold 99th <=350ms at peak with target QPS we need ~14 GPU stream slots (concurrent ) per 100 qps; that maps to 8 GPUs for steady-state and 16 GPUs for peak with headroom.

I attached the sizing profile I used: sizing-profile-arbor-16gpu.json (note: this is a conservative model — Karhik we should re-run with your sequence length distributions).

Operational plan (short):
1) Week 0-1: Provision 6 GPUs (40% of target), deploy model variant v1.2-quant, smoke tests with 10% staged traffic.
2) Week 2-4: Progressively route 30% -> 60% traffic; run throughput ramp tests, enable KV cache warm-up.
3) Week 5-6: Full routing (100%) for steady-state validation. DNS TTL drop and final cutover in maintenance window.

If we observe token TTF regressions or 99th >350ms for more than 15 minutes, auto-fallback to hosted will be triggered and we pause further traffic increases.

—Jordan
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Reed <ereed@arborlabs.ai>, Nora Kim <nora.kim@arborlabs.ai>
Date: 2026-09-24 09:02 PDT
Subject: Re: Arbor onramp — contract & throttle language + acceptance gates

Adding contract and acceptance perspective:
- We can bind a 6-month reserved commit but recommend a 30-day ramp clause: initial effective capacity billed at 50% for first 30 days while we validate. This eases Arbor's cashflow and aligns incentives.
- Acceptance gates: performance (99th latency), error rate <=0.3%, throughput within +/-10% of forecast. If any gate fails after 3 retries, fallback and remediation window opens.
- SLA exception: define one planned maintenance cutover (2-hour window) during which we may route back to hosted temporarily.

Marcus — please capture these points into the cutover-window-checklist.pdf (I added comments inline).

—Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Arbor onramp — cutover checklist draft (v0.3)

Attached is v0.3 of the cutover checklist. Highlights:
- Pre-cutover (48-72h): smoke test plan, KV cache pre-warm steps, baseline perf snapshot, and rollback playbook.
- Cutover window (2h): progressive DNS shift (three phases), monitoring dashboards live, SRE oncall + Redwood infra lead, and contact list for Arbor.
- Post-cutover (72h): validation plan, token-level cost reconciliation, and a 1-week observations cadence.

Ethan — can Arbor commit to an initial 2-hour maintenance window on the evening of Oct 6th (PST)? That would let us do the TTL drop and final cutover with minimal user impact.

Attachment: cutover-window-checklist.pdf

—Marcus
Infrastructure Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
